The *Vaṅgīsattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 546) is a Pali verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages, though it registers no established historical parallels [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus identify 211 matching passages shared across 33 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs within the commentarial tradition, particularly the second part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares an extensive run of verses (notably §1.1–25.3), as well as the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the first part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and thematic parallels are also shared extensively with other Apadāna poems, including the *Kaṅkhārevatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 544), *Kisāgotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 22), *Soṇātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 26), and *Lakuṇḍabhaddiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 543) [DharmaNexus].

Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with several non-Pali Buddhist corpora, including the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (長阿含經, T 1), the Tibetan translation of the *Avadānaśataka* (*Pūrṇapramukha-avadānaśataka*, D0343), the alternative Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* translation (別譯雜阿含經, T 100), the *Shouxinsui jing* (受新歲經, T 61), and the Chinese *Ekottarikāgama* (增壹阿含經, T 125) [DharmaNexus].
